item.title: The Best of Us
item.content:encoded: I don’t particularly care for Dolly Parton’s music, but I loved Dolly Parton. She was literally the best of us. Unapologetically herself whether people liked it or not. Did not give a single fuck about what was “expected” of her based on her age, gender, career aspirations, and so on. Could have been a billionaire, but chose to invest tremendous amounts of money in communities that were underserved instead. A highly visible counter-argument to the idea that older white cishetero folks can’t help being racist, sexist, and homophobic because of when and where they grew up.

item.title: Make Care Visible
item.content:encoded: There’s a rather popular flavor of social media content focused on helping unhoused people. The creator will give out sleeping bags, socks, and care kits; sit down and have a meal; or take the unhoused person shopping. Sometimes they help them find work or start a GoFundMe to get them off the streets. It does a lot of good. But it’s also gross AF! Imagine you’re cold, hungry, and desperate, and someone offers to get you all the things you need… if you consent to having a camera shoved in your face and the footage of you at your lowest blasted on the internet.

item.title: How to apply CSS only if there are a certain number of nested elements
item.content:encoded: This week, I had to write CSS for a design where a list of elements got a bit of extra design treatment if there were at least three nested items inside it. <!-- Base design --> <ul class="magic-list"> <li>Item 1</li> <li>Item 2</li> </ul> <!-- Extra design --> <ul class="magic-list"> <li>Item 1</li> <li>Item 2</li> <li>Item 3</li> <li>Item 4</li> <!-- ... --> </ul> I really wanted to avoid using JavaScript to add/remove an extra class, and the the :has() pseudo-class and the nth-* pseudo-class made it shockingly easy!

item.title: On fresh starts
item.content:encoded: Back in March, I shared a bit of a sad update on my unhoused friends. Cops raided their camp and took everything they owned. Within the week… Mike had relapsed Manny got arrested for stealing copper Ron was all by himself But last Friday, I got an amazing phone call from Mike! Sometime over the winter, he checked himself into rehab. He’s several months clean now. He’s doing therapy to address the trauma that’s caused him to use.

item.title: The spirit of giving
item.content:encoded: I’m a huge fan of the Buy Nothing Project, a movement that promotes the sharing and giving economy over one where people buy ever more shit. The spirit of Buy Nothing is sharing with your neighbors. It’s wonderful. But as it’s popularity in my area has grown, I’ve noticed that some folks have started using it as a way to just offload shit they’re too lazy to drive to a donation spot or throw away.

item.title: Propaganda
item.content:encoded: The album Let’s Get Free by Dead Prez came out 26 years ago. As a teen, it spoke to my angst. As a whole ass adult, its wild to look back on it and realize just how much nuance and bigger picture I missed in their lyrics. Yesterday, their song “Propaganda” came on a random playlist I was listening to… You can’t fool all the people all of the time

item.title: Rebuilding communities
item.content:encoded: The video Constructing the Revolution talks about how to start prefiguring the future you want today. (Heads up: the middle section of the video gets into some pretty heavy territory.) Early on, there’s some important conversation about rebuilding and repairing communities that have been shattered by a system that deliberately pits us against one another. All hierarchies of power desire to keep us separate, competing, and individualistic, because because we’re easier to exploit that way.
